Changelog

2.0.10 adds a per-node session limit policy, quiets device-limit and takeover alerts, removes new user defaults and adds a days-or-date expiry control; 2.0.9 completes the audit fix for panels upgraded from older releases; 2.0.8 restores billing after a panel rebuild, creates the audit trail directory and makes surplus session rows read as pending; 2.0.6 makes a node upgrade turn live push on without a panel restart; 2.0.5 adds live session and usage updates over a per-node event stream; 2.0.4 serves the panel's precompressed assets; 2.0.3 fixes updates on IP-certificate panels; 2.0.2 fixes Let's Encrypt IP issuance; 2.0.1 restores built-in issuance and automatic renewal. 2.0.0 is the first supported release; there is no upgrade path from pre-2.0.0 builds, and everything below it is archived history.

2.0.10 - 2026-11-13

  • Session limit policy per node. Choose strict (refuse at the limit), reserve (one temporary reconnect slot, released after the grace) or takeover (replace one existing session). One-device users keep the takeover path. The policy is stored beside the node state and applies on the next connection without an OpenVPN restart. Requires OVNode 2.0.19.
  • Quieter alerts. Device-limit rejections and takeover failures no longer create a toast or a topbar alert, and a user who is simply using their allowed devices no longer produces an alert. Takeover failures are warnings, not authentication failures. The Security page groups repeated events by user, node and reason with a count.
  • New users start unlimited. The New User Defaults section is removed. A new user has no expiry, no traffic cap and unlimited devices unless the operator fills a field. An empty expiry is accepted on update, and zero traffic means unlimited.
  • Expiry by days or date. The user form now switches between a day count and a date. Empty means never expires. The calendar button opens the native date picker, and dates use local time so the stored day does not shift.

2.0.9 — 2026-11-13

  • Audit trail on existing installs. 2.0.8 provisioned the audit directory from the unit and the updater, but an update runs the previously installed updater, so a panel upgraded from 2.0.4/2.0.7 could still have an unwritable /var/log/ovmanager. When that directory is not writable the trail now uses DataDir/audit.jsonl (the same service owner) and every process picks the same file — the Logs page fills immediately after the upgrade.

2.0.8 — 2026-11-13

  • Billing after a panel rebuild. Traffic totals are matched to users by certificate CN name as well as by numeric id, so nodes that still carry pre-rebuild certificates bill again instead of reporting billed 0 bytes forever.
  • Audit trail. The panel creates and owns /var/log/ovmanager (unit LogsDirectory plus an updater ownership fix) and logs one warning when it cannot write, instead of silently dropping entries and leaving the Logs page empty.
  • Session limits. A failed or expired session the node has not reaped yet reads +N pending instead of an alarming over-limit count; the tooltip explains it is released automatically.

2.0.7 — 2026-11-12

  • Offline detection on streams. A node whose stream is down now has its drop re-applied on every retry, so the 20-second grace window expires and the badge turns red instead of staying green until the node returns.

2.0.6 — 2026-11-12

  • Node upgrades take effect on their own. A node that answered the event stream with 404 is re-probed every five minutes instead of never, so updating it to OVNode 2.0.15 turns live push on without restarting the panel. The fallback log line still appears once per node, and the re-probe is one request per node per five minutes.

2.0.5 — 2026-11-12

  • Live dashboard updates. The panel opens one event stream per node (the new GET /sync/events endpoint in OVNode 2.0.15). Session changes reach the browser in a fraction of a second, usage counters refresh every 10 seconds, and steady-state node polling for the live view stops while a stream is open.
  • Polling fallback. A node older than 2.0.15 answers the stream with 404 once; the panel keeps its existing polling path for that node, so the panel can be upgraded before the nodes.
  • Monitoring UI. Green live dots for users and nodes, usage bars fed by the live counter between billing passes, connect/disconnect/reject toasts, and an online-user count in the topbar.
  • Billing unchanged. Live events are display-only: traffic accounting still comes from the 60-second cumulative-delta pass, so an upgrade can never change a bill.

2.0.4 — 2026-11-12

  • Faster first dashboard load. The panel now serves the SPA build's precompressed .gz siblings when the browser accepts gzip: the main JS bundle drops from about 395 KB to 122 KB, and the CSS from 43 KB to 8.8 KB. Cached assets are unchanged; this is the cold-first-visit path.

2.0.3 — 2026-11-12

  • Updates on an IP-certificate panel. The health probe prefers the loopback response that reports the version, so a panel serving HTTPS for its public IP no longer fails verification with ? and rolls back.
  • Installer updates. The installer's Update downloads the target release and runs that release's updater, so a fix in the new version is not gated behind the installed copy.

2.0.2 — 2026-11-12

  • IP certificates. Omit the IP address from the CSR Common Name; Let's Encrypt rejects an IP in the CN (badCSR) and requires it in the subjectAltName instead. Verified against Let's Encrypt production on an IP-only server.

2.0.1 — 2026-11-12

  • HTTPS certificates. The built-in ACME client is back: Let's Encrypt for a domain or the server's public IPv4 (short-lived profile), issued by the installer or ovmanager tls acme. The panel renews daily with a lifetime-based window and reloads the new pair without a restart.
  • Installer. The same-server OVNode step uses the node's release bootstrap instead of a stale pinned script; install defaults to the wizard on a terminal; a failed node step no longer reports a full success.
  • Panel update. The updater stages ovmanager-server and its symlink, so a 2.0.1 update does not leave the unit pointing at a missing binary.

2.0.0 — 2026-11-11

  • Reset line. Database baseline is app.db with a single schema.sql; the 38-step migration history, legacy table adoption and pre-2.0.0 state formats are gone. A pre-2.0.0 database is refused, not migrated.
  • Node protocol. Nodes run UDP, TCP, or both. both starts one OpenVPN process per transport on the same port, and profiles carry a connection block per protocol and port.
  • Node settings. OpenVPN tuning lives in state/openvpn.json and is edited from the node drawer: max clients, keepalive, redirect, DNS, routes, IPv6, MTU/mssfix, ciphers, TLS floor, renegotiation, idle timeout, verbosity. The node validates, regenerates and reloads, rolling back a failed apply.
  • Configuration. Panel .env uses PascalCase keys; node .env is 12. No product prefixes, no reverse-proxy mode, no forwarded-header trust, no DATABASE_URL keys. TLS keys are TlsCertFile/TlsKeyFile.
  • Security. Node TLS pins are required (the unverified fallback is gone); backup archives are framed and capped; the node rate limiter sweeps on a timer; profiles never carry another node's address or panel_domain; the panel journal endpoint is limited to its own unit.
  • Installer. One Go installer (the bash fallback is deleted), typed exit codes, checksum-gated bootstrap, ovnode update resolves latest, and per-instance host files (logrotate, cron, sysctl, NAT, backups).

Archived: pre-reset line

2.0.4 — 2026-11-11

  • Storage refactor: billing package renamed to accounting; traffic simplified to a User.used overwrite (baselines/epochs dropped); settings_kv merged into settings; PascalCase tables; sessions moved in-memory.
  • Admin roles base: role column with the owner role set.
  • NodeStat time-series (cpu/memory/live_count per node).
  • Backup expansion: panel pulls the node backup archive; Telegram upload with optional AES-256 at-rest encryption; Google Drive target via rclone.
  • Node undo for deletes; audit events PascalCase; contract.json restored as a derived artifact.
  • CI/toolchain: gosec findings cleared, Go 1.27.4 and govulncheck pinned, corrupted action pins repaired, staticcheck and deadcode wired into lint.

2.0.3 — 2026-11-09

  • Telegram activation tokens: private-chat redemption, per-chat rate limiting, schema migration.
  • Full bot UX: command menu, rich welcome, /help, /nodes, /balance, config send, inline keyboards, callback queries, edited-message handling.
  • Panel hardening: bot token masked and never persisted plaintext, Telegram rate limit restored, Origin-required cookie mutations, XFF left-most walk, loopback-only trusted CIDRs, request body caps, password min 12 / reject over 72 bytes, hex secret keys, subscription path validation, API 404 bodies preserved.
  • SPA serving fixes: root serving when the URL prefix is empty, subscription links never inherit the dashboard prefix, single error boundary, backdrop keeps form drafts, login response envelope accepted.

2.0.2

  • Wire-contract v3 negotiation and panel compat banner.
  • Undo TTL raised and tested; restore stamps user_version; newer-schema rejection.
  • ZIP bulk download skips disabled users (policy-first push kept).
  • Feature cuts: ACME worker, geolocation, Telegram daemon (later restored as in-panel bot).
  • Single systemd unit for the node; Go dedup; contract generation in CI.

2.0.1 — 2026-11-05

  • Checksum/signature verification removed from installer, release workflows, and update CLI; releases ship bare binaries.
  • Installer and docs fetch install.sh from main (latest).

2.0.0 pre-reset build — 2026-11-02

  • Native systemd service architecture (ovmanager-server) with hybrid operator CLI (ovmanager).
  • Docker deployment removed.
  • Standalone single-file installer (install.sh) with inlined runtime libraries.
  • Refactored update pipeline with validation and rollback.
  • Owner-only administrative model.

Pre-reset (archived)
